data.title: Delek US Holdings to Host Third Quarter 2026 Conference Call on November 6, 2026
data.description:
Delek US Holdings, Inc. () (“Delek US”) today announced that the Company intends to issue a press release summarizing third quarter 2026 results before the U.S. stock market opens on Friday, November 6, 2026. A conference call to discuss these results is scheduled to begin at 10:00 a.m. CT (11:00 a.m. ET) on Friday, November 6, 2026.

The live broadcast of this conference call will be available online by going to www.DelekUS.com and clicking on the investor relations section of the website. A presentation containing supplemental financial information will also be available online at ir.delekus.com prior to the conference call and webcast. The Company does not intend to furnish this presentation on a Current Report on Form 8-K. Investors are encouraged to review the presentation in conjunction with the Company’s earnings press release and webcast. The online replay will be available on the website for 90 days.

About Delek US Holdings, Inc.

Delek US Holdings, Inc. is a diversified downstream energy company with assets in petroleum refining, logistics, pipelines, and renewable fuels. The refining assets consist primarily of refineries operated in Tyler and Big Spring, Texas, El Dorado, Arkansas and Krotz Springs, Louisiana with a combined nameplate crude throughput capacity of 302,000 barrels per day.

The logistics operations include Delek Logistics Partners, LP (). Delek Logistics Partners, LP is a growth-oriented master limited partnership focused on owning and operating midstream energy infrastructure assets. Delek US Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiaries owned approximately 58.0% (including the general partner interest) of Delek Logistics Partners, LP as of September 30, 2026.

Information about Delek US Holdings, Inc. can be found on its website (www.delekus.com), investor relations webpage (ir.delekus.com), and news webpage (www.delekus.com/news).

data.title: ICE review: Canola Weakens on Seasonal Harvest Pressure
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--The ICE Futures canola market was weaker on Friday, hitting fresh seven-week lows as steady farmer selling and bearish technical signals weighed on prices.

  • November canola was down by C$2.90 at C$798.80 per ton, with the move below C$800 per ton bearish from a chart standpoint.
  • Losses in the Chicago soy complex and European rapeseed contributed to the softer tone in canola, although Malaysian palm oil was firmer to end the week.
  • Seasonal harvest pressure remained a bearish influence, as warm and dry forecasts across most of the Prairies this weekend should allow farmers to make good progress bringing in the last of the crop.
  • Farmers delivered 620,100 tons of canola into the commercial pipeline during the week ended Oct. 11, reported the Canadian Grain Commission. While that was down by 19% from the previous week, crop-year-to-date deliveries at 4.45 million tons are 28% ahead of last year's pace.
  • Weekly Canadian canola exports at 158,300 tons were down from 248,400 tons the previous week. Crop-year-to-date exports are up 44% on the year at 1.38 million tons through 10 weeks.
  • There were 113,995 contracts traded on Friday, which compares with Thursday when 107,034 contracts changed hands. Spreading accounted for 81,200 of the contracts traded.

data.title: SoftBank weighs $18 billion acquisition of Allied Universal, Bloomberg News reports
data.description:
SoftBank Group is considering an acquisition of Allied Universal in a deal that could value the US security services provider at about $18 billion, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

  • Allied Universal provides security staffing for businesses, venues and major events, and has a growing presence in the data center industry, supporting both development and operation of facilities

  • The potential acquisition would complement SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son's increasing focus on AI, as he is exploring the use of AI-powered robots across industries, and looking to strengthen the infrastructure needed to support the technology, according to the report

  • With Allied, SoftBank would look to eventually replace some staff with robots to handle security work, the report said, citing one of the people

  • The application of humanoid-like security workers will likely take more time, it reported citing another person

  • Deliberations are preliminary and no final decisions have been made, including on the potential price, the report said

  • SoftBank declined to comment on the report, while Allied Universal did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment

  • SoftBank is widely known for making large technology investments through its Vision Fund. It was an early investor in Alibaba, owns a majority stake in Arm, and was a major backer of the office-sharing startup WeWork

  • In October, SoftBank completed the final phase of its planned $30 billion investment in OpenAI, deepening its commitment to the AI company

data.title: Apparel retailer True Religion explores sale, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • JPMorgan is running the process, which is at an early stage
  • Company's annual earnings approach $150 million, revenue close to $550 million
  • ACON Investments acquired True Religion in 2024

By Abigail Summerville

Clothing retailer True Religion is exploring options including a full sale or minority stake sale that could value the brand, known for its denim, at close to $1 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

The company, owned by ACON Investments, is working with JPMorgan on the process, which is at an early stage, the people said, requesting anonymity to discuss a confidential matter.

ACON acquired True Religion almost two years ago, and since then the company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) have nearly doubled, approaching $150 million annually, the people said. The brand generates close to $550 million of annual revenue, they said.

True Religion, ACON and JPMorgan declined to comment.

Founded in 2002, True Religion launched in Los Angeles as a premium jeans brand popular with celebrities and known for its bold "Super T" stitching. Fifteen years later, it went bankrupt twice, in 2017 and then during the pandemic in 2020, as consumer tastes shifted away from denim and towards athleisure and more affordable brands.

True Religion now offers lower-priced denim and a broader range of products across categories, genders and age groups.

Jeans account for 35% to 40% of its revenue, its CEO Michael Buckley said on a podcast this month. The company describes itself as an "urban casual lifestyle brand" and has benefited from shoppers' nostalgia for early 2000s style.

The El Segundo, California-based company operates around 60 brick-and-mortar stores with a goal to hit 150 stores, Buckley said on the podcast.

ACON acquired a controlling stake in the business in December 2024 alongside SB360 Capital Partners, an affiliate of the Schottenstein family, veterans of the retail industry. Jay Schottenstein, chairman of SB360, serves as CEO of American Eagle Outfitters .

data.title: Treasury Yields Fall in Week as Turmoil Subsides — Market Talk
data.description:
1552 ET - Treasury yields fall this week as bond markets turbulence subsides. Fed officials signal no rush to raise rates, while Chairman Warsh stays away from guidance. Derivatives indicate investors' one-year inflation expectations drift away from the Fed's 2% target and reach 2.64%, the highest since June, according to LSEG. U.S. industrial production increases more than expected in September. Oil rises 3.5%. The 30-year has its largest weekly decline since April 2025, falling 0.162 percentage point to 5.436%. The 10-year falls 0.146 point to 5.097% and is down for two consecutive weeks. The two-year sheds 0.055 point to 4.734%, down for three straight weeks. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1331 ET - Major cryptocurrencies are weaker, with sizably-lower volumes seen in afternoon trading, according to data from Coinglass. Trading volumes for bitcoin over the past 24 hours are off 39%, to $49.2 billion. Other tokens are seeing larger decreases in volume, with ethereum volume off 42% to $34.3 billion, HYPE volume down 41% to $1.8 billion, and XRP falling 42% to $2.1 billion. Outflows in bitcoin futures have picked up in the last 5 minutes, according to Coinglass--with outflows seen at $75.2 million and inflows at $31 million. Bitcoin is down 1% to $81,177, ethereum falls 1.3% to $2,419, and XRP slides 2.8% to $1.30. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

1235 ET - Weaker activity will likely give Brazil's central bank room to keep cutting its hefty interest rates, TS Lombard's João Pedro Oliveira Fachetti says in a note. He expects the BCB to shave a quarter of a percentage point on November 4 and another in December, bringing the Selic rate to 13.25% by year end, while "further cuts hinge on the approval of structural reforms." President Lula da Silva faces right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro in the final round of vote on October 25 in a tight race. Bolsonaro is seen as a fiscal hawk and Fachetti says his eventual victory could strengthen the Brazilian real, helping contain inflationary pressures. The real climbs 0.3% against the dollar. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1139 ET - Solana, the crypto token with the fifth-largest market capitalization in the market, excluding stablecoins, is supported by a transaction speed that's exponentially higher than its competitors, says Zach Pandl of Grayscale in a note. Pandl says that solana averages roughly 1,400 transactions per second, well exceeding the next-fastest competitor Binance Coins's 200 transactions per second, and other crypto tokens at speeds of roughly 40 transactions per second. Solana's transaction speed is scheduled to accelerate next week with the introduction of its so-called 'Alpenglow' upgrade, which Pandl says will put the token further ahead as a blockchain for developers to use speed-wise. After trading higher earlier in the day, solana is now down 1.3% to $104.17. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

1120 ET - A weaker USD index is giving many major cryptocurrencies support. This week has seen bitcoin and other crypto tokens responding more to macro market moves and less to how tech and AI stocks move, says Colin Basco of Coinbase Institutional in a note. "Bitcoin's correlation with chip stocks has also fallen to well under half its January peak, indicating that the market is no longer treating bitcoin as a leveraged proxy for technology stocks," says Basco. He adds that spot demand for bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies remains the "soft spot" for prices, especially as odds for a rate hike before the end of the month are seen rising. Bitcoin is up 0.1% to $82,106, while ethereum rises 0.4% to $2,460. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

1109 ET - A solid rise in U.S. industrial production in September still leaves some lukewarm indicators. Production rises 0.7% in the month. Citi's Veronica Clark and Andrew Hollenhorst say in a note that "manufacturing production has moved mostly sideways since the spring and remains below production levels of 2014-18." They add that manufacturing production rose "a more modest" 0.3%. "While strong AI-demand has boosted business investment, much of this investment is imported, implying domestic production has not been as strong," Clark and Hollenhorst say. They add that higher interest rates and fading fiscal support represent headwinds to non-AI manufacturing into 2027. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1033 ET - Unlike in recent years, the British economy has sustained its early-year momentum into the second half of 2026, Oxford Economics' Andrew Goodwin says in a note. "This likely reflects a combination of genuine strength due to structural change because of IT-related investment, but also noisy data," he says. Rapid increases in AI usage mean recent IT strength will likely endure, though strong pickup in professional services output in the last six months is harder to explain. Any resilience will come under pressure over the next few quarters, particularly given most of the impact of the Middle East war is still to come. Financial conditions have worsened, and fiscal policy is being tightened, he adds. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)

1026 ET - If Albertans and Quebecois did vote to leave Canada, what would that mean for the rest of the country? Capital Economics' Bradley Saunders argues the blow to GDP from losing Quebec industry and Alberta oil and gas could be mediated somewhat by continued free trade, companies relocating from seceding provinces to the rest of Canada and a weaker Canadian dollar boosting export competitiveness in other sectors. As such, the economist expects the rest of Canada to outperform the two provinces, whose newfound independence would likely require fiscal tightening. Of course secession would be a lengthy and complicated process without precedent and as such there remains a lot of uncertainty, Saunders says. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1026 ET - Canada's housing market remains soft, with a combination of higher fixed mortgage rates and potential Bank of Canada tightening likely keeping buyers on the defensive, Bank of Montreal's Robert Kavcic says. The economist continues to argue that market pricing of a percentage point in interest rates increases in 2027 is too aggressive, but says the balance of risk is tilting to the upside for variable rates into the coming spring market for housing. "This poses an issue for the market given that variable rates are currently the lowest available by a relatively wide margin, and most buyers have pivoted to that space," he says. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1024 ET - Elevated oil prices boosted Canada's purchasing power but the gains are uneven across the country, Royal Bank of Canada says. Real gross domestic income expanded 3.1% on-year in 2Q, nearly triple the pace of real GDP growth after a 46% surge in oil added about C$12 billion a quarter to export revenue. Royal Bank says oil producers and resource-rich provinces are capturing a disproportionate share of the initial windfall, while most households face higher costs without offsetting income gains. This complicates monetary policy, since the Bank of Canada controls only one interest rate for the entire country, Royal Bank adds. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1018 ET - The rise in mortgage rates has sent Canada's housing market into reverse, with sales and prices both falling in September, says Capital Economics' Stephen Brown. With the risk mortgage rate rise further prices could fall a bit more in the coming months, though Brown doesn't anticipate the Bank of Canada will lift its policy rate as aggressively as markets are pricing in. Lenders have been forced to pass on higher funding costs to fixed mortgage rates. Yet while home prices may fall near term, Brown says he is more upbeat about the outlook from mid-2027 as mortgage rates drop back next year. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1011 ET - The widening of spreads between French and German government bond yields has had as much, or possibly more, negative impact on the euro as widening Treasury-German spreads, Standard Chartered's Steve Englander says in a note. "Rising French credit default swaps (CDS) also have a significant impact on euro; although the relationship is not as tight as with the French-German spread, the CDS correlation still supports the view of concerns about France's government finances." The euro faces renewed depreciation if spreads widen further, he says. The euro rises 0.3% to $1.1256 after hitting a 17-month low of $1.1112 Wednesday, LSEG data show. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

data.title: Canadian Securities Exchange Reports September 2026 Performance Figures

  • Trading value of CSE listed securities was $376 million;

This two-day event brings together mining companies, brokers, and investors for keynote presentations and valuable networking opportunities with industry peers. data.title: Air Canada, United to add routes, increase flight capacity in 2027
data.description:
Air Canada and United Airlines plan to expand their Canada-US networks next summer, adding new routes and increasing flight capacity under a transborder partnership that the carriers have agreed to renew, subject to regulatory approval.

Air Canada will introduce service from Toronto to Louisville on April 28, 2027, followed by flights from Montreal to Indianapolis and Edmonton to Newark beginning June 1. It will also deploy larger Airbus A220 aircraft on its Edmonton-San Francisco route to increase capacity.

United plans seasonal flights between Newark and St. John's, Newfoundland, and new services linking Denver with Ottawa and Quebec City. The carrier will also increase flights between Washington, D.C., and Quebec City and boost daily seats between Denver and Winnipeg by 65%.

The expansion builds on a joint business agreement established in 2022 that has enabled 20 new transborder routes, according to Air Canada . The partnership supports more than 1,200 connecting itineraries between Canada and the United States.

Air Canada said an application seeking approval of the renewed and expanded agreement had been submitted to Transport Canada.

The carriers said the additional services would broaden travel options and improve connections through their respective networks. The announcement comes amid softer cross-border demand in recent months.

data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    October 16, 2026, Montreal, Quebec, Canada – TheNewswire - Beauce Gold Fields (“Champs d’Or en Beauce”) (TSX Venture: BGF), referred to as “BGF” or the “Company,” is closing a non-brokered Flow-Through private placement of 6,649,00 units at $0.035 per unit for gross proceeds of $232,715.00.

    Each unit will comprise one Flow-Through common share and one-half common share purchase warrant of the company. Each full warrant will entitle the holder thereof to purchase one common share of the capital stock of the company at a price of S0.07 for a period of 24 months from the date of closing of the placement. Securities issued under the placement are subject to a four-month-and-one-day hold period from the date of closing of the placement in accordance with applicable Canadian securities laws. The placement is subject to standard regulatory approvals, including the approval of the TSX Venture Exchange. The proceeds of the placement will be used: (i) to finance exploration.

    In connection with the placement, the company will pay finders' fees of $6,938.40. It will also issue 198,240 warrants to the agents. The warrants will entitle the agents to purchase one common share of the capital stock of the company at a price of S0.07 for a period of 24 months from the date of closing of the placement. All shares issued on those warrants exercise will be subject to a four-month-and-one-day hold period from the date of closing of the placement.

    An Insider of the company subscribed for 300,000 units in the placement.   Ann Levasseur, a Director of the Company, subscribed for 300,000 flow-through units. As a result, Ann Levasseur will beneficially own or exercise control or direction over, directly or indirectly, 932,606 shares representing 0.618% of the issued and outstanding common shares of the company.

    The participation of Ann Levasseur in the private placement constitutes a related party transaction within the meaning of Multilateral Instrument 61-101 — Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions, and TSX Venture Exchange Policy 5.9 — Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions. In connection with this related party transaction, the company is relying on the formal valuation and minority approval exemptions of subsections 5.5(a) and 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101, respectively, as the fair market value of the portion of the private placement subscribed by insiders does not exceed 25 per cent of the company's market capitalization. The board of directors of the company has approved the private placement, including the participation of said Ann Levasseur.

    The company will use the proceeds from the private placement for exploration of its gold and phosphate properties.

    About the Saint-Simon-les-Mines Paleoplacer Channel

    The Saint-Simon-les-Mines paleoplacer is a nearly six-kilometre-long buried gold-bearing channel within the Gilbert River paleovalley and represents the core of Canada’s first gold rush district. Historical mining from the 1860s through the 1960s recovered significant quantities of coarse gold, including multi-ounce nuggets.

    The Company’s geological model indicates that gold mineralization within the paleoplacer system is concentrated principally within basal sedimentary horizons, saprolitic bedrock and fractures or natural traps developed along the paleovalley floor

    The paleovalley lies immediately south of the Company’s interpreted Saddle Reef-style antiform structures. BGF’s geological model is evaluating these structures and associated quartz-vein systems as potential bedrock sources for at least part of the historical placer gold.

    Historical and modern geological work also indicates that tributaries entering the Gilbert River paleovalley from the north may have played an important role in transporting and concentrating gold. Interpreted deltaic deposits developed at tributary mouths therefore represent priority exploration targets for the sonic drilling program.

    More information:

    https://beaucegold.com/beauce-gold-property

    Click Image To View Full Size

    Image: Polygonal - Longitudinal Map of the Paleoplacer Channel

    Exploration Target

    The drilling program follows the Company’s June 2026 technical assessment of the Saint-Simon-les-Mines paleoplacer channel, which established an Exploration Target ranging between:

    • 4,004,674 and 5,991,229 cubic metres; and


    • 2.02 g Au/m³ to 12.0 g Au/m³


    The Exploration Target is based on the interpretation of historical drilling, geological modelling and reconstruction of the Gilbert River paleovalley, polygonal volumetric calculations, and the evaluation of auriferous basal sedimentary, saprolitic and weathered bedrock units.

    The updated geological interpretation recognizes the potential importance of buried tributaries and deltaic deposits, natural bedrock traps and greater-than-previously-recognized thicknesses of saprolitic and fractured bedrock within the paleovalley.

    The potential quantity and grade of the Exploration Target are conceptual in nature. There has been insufficient exploration to define a mineral resource, and it is uncertain whether further exploration will result in the delineation of a mineral resource.

    Jean Bernard, B.Sc., P.Geo., an independent Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101, has reviewed and approved the technical content of this news release.

    About Beauce Gold Fields

    Beauce Gold Fields is focused on exploring and developing the historic placer gold district of the Beauce region of southern Quebec. The Company’s objective is to trace historical placer gold workings back to potential bedrock sources and evaluate the potential for economic lode-gold mineralization.

    The Company’s flagship property is the Saint-Simon-les-Mines gold project, site of Canada’s first gold rush, which predates the Yukon Klondike. The Beauce region hosted major historical placer gold operations from the 1860s through the 1960s and produced some of the largest gold nuggets recorded in Canadian mining history, including nuggets exceeding 50 ounces. (Source: SEDAR, NI 43-101 Report – Beauce, July 4, 2018, author B. Violette.)

    Beauce Gold Fields continues to explore antiform structures that the Company believes may have contributed gold to the extensive auriferous placer deposits of the Beauce region. The Company’s geological model is evaluating whether structural traps associated with antiform folding and saddle-reef-style quartz mineralization may represent potential bedrock sources for gold found within the historical Beauce paleoplacer system.

data.title: Oil Futures Rise on Middle East, Russia-Ukraine Concerns — 3rd Update
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid and Anthony Harrup

Oil prices rose Friday after Ukraine renewed attacks on Russian refineries, adding to concerns about persistent Middle East supply risks and uncertainty over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude for December delivery settled up 3.7% at $109.86 a barrel, and December West Texas Intermediate gained 2.6% to $99.02 a barrel. Front-month WTI for November rose 3.5% to $101.41 a barrel, topping the $100 mark for the first time in a month.

"The main reason is that Ukraine has renewed its attacks on Russian oil refineries," said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital. "Despite the IEA and its member countries having already released approximately 300 million barrels from emergency oil reserves, with another 100 million barrels likely to be released, prices continue to rise."

The International Energy Agency said Thursday that its members agreed to accelerate the release of around 100 million barrels of previously pledged emergency oil stocks, including more than 20 million barrels of diesel to be released as soon as possible.

About 330 million barrels have already been released, and the agency said total releases would exceed the 400 million barrels initially agreed upon in March, with some members contributing additional volumes.

"We're still in a bull market," said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president of trading at BOK Financial. Flows through the Strait of Hormuz aren't reliable, expectations of Russian diesel coming onto the market aren't being met, and with Ukrainian attacks on refineries "those barrels are going to have trouble getting to the market," he said.

A third factor is that demand destruction "at least in the U.S. is not happening," he added.

Despite recovering Middle East oil flows, uncertainty surrounding the conflict continues to support crude prices, analysts at ING said. The bank said a sustained recovery in shipments through the Strait of Hormuz could gradually reduce the geopolitical risk premium, but a U.S.-Iran agreement would be needed to give markets greater confidence that higher flows could be maintained.

However, oil prices above $100 a barrel appear increasingly stretched relative to market fundamentals, according to Norbert Rucker, head of economics and next generation research at Julius Baer. Middle Eastern exports have largely recovered and global inventories remain comfortable, while geopolitical risk premiums and elevated freight costs could ease, he said.

"The relative calm in oil markets seems untenable, as the gradual recovery in Middle East oil flows has come under pressure of late from a resurgence of attacks on shipping," Barclays analyst Amarpreet Singh said in a note. "What looked like a tail risk scenario a few weeks ago--in which a diplomatic resolution takes us back to pre-war levels of Middle East supply and spare capacity--looks an even more remote possibility at this point," he added.

Shipping risks remain high after two cargo ships sank near the Strait of Hormuz following attacks, The Wall Street Journal reported. U.K. Maritime Trade Operations separately reported Wednesday that two container ships were struck by unidentified projectiles while transiting the waterway.

Risks to shipping have pushed up freight and insurance costs, contributing to the higher price of oil.

War-risk premiums add several million dollars per shipment to the cost of moving oil from Hormuz to somewhere else in the world, said Dennis Marvin, head of marine at insurer MSIG USA.

"It's probably as volatile as it has been, and my answer is it's getting worse," he said, noting the addition of Houthi attacks in the Red Sea and the conflict with Saudi Arabia to the situation in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman. "I can't even perceive when the calm is going to come next. I don't see this changing anytime soon."

Write to Farhan Rafid at farhan.rafid@wsj.com and Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com

data.title: Fujitsu Japan to offer cloud-native electronic health record system compliant with Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's standard specifications and certification program
data.description:
KAWASAKI, Japan, Oct 16, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Fujitsu Japan Limited today announced that it has commenced specification compliance and functional enhancements for its cloud-native electronic health record (EHR) system [1], currently under development, effective October 16, 2026. This initiative follows the public announcement of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's (MHLW) standard specifications and certification program for EHR systems targeting clinics and small to medium-sized hospitals. Fujitsu Japan aims to launch this cloud-native EHR system in April 2027, leveraging digital technology to address regional medical challenges and realize a society where sustainable healthcare is provided.

Clinics and small to medium-sized hospitals, which are vital to regional healthcare, often face numerous concerns when introducing EHR systems. These include selecting a system suitable for their operations, securing initial implementation and operational costs, a shortage of IT personnel, and managing security risks. Fujitsu Japan will address these challenges by developing and providing an easy-to-use and secure cloud-native EHR system. Furthermore, the system is planned to integrate with various national healthcare digital transformation (DX) services, including the electronic prescription service and the electronic health record information sharing service [2].

Through these efforts, Fujitsu Japan aims to contribute to the widespread adoption of cloud-native EHR systems for small to medium-sized hospitals, facilitating patient information sharing, improving operational efficiency, and enhancing medical services in healthcare institutions.

Looking ahead, Fujitsu Japan plans to offer a highly scalable cloud-native EHR system for large hospitals by fiscal year 2028 [3], enabling flexible integration with external services such as AI and other healthcare systems. The system will respond rapidly to regulatory changes and advances in healthcare DX while enabling the continuous delivery of the latest functionality and advanced security measures. The company is currently participating in the Council for the Modernization of Hospital Information Systems, convened and promoted by the Digital Agency and MHLW, and is advancing development in collaboration with the government. As a top vendor holding a 47% market share in the large hospital sector [4] with solutions such as "Fujitsu Healthcare Solution HOPE LifeMark-HX Cloud," Fujitsu Japan will consolidate its expertise. This will accelerate DX in healthcare settings through enhanced cybersecurity, utilization of medical data, and the application of technologies like generative AI, thereby contributing to the realization of a safe, secure, and sustainable healthcare delivery system.

[1] Cloud-native electronic health record (EHR) system:

An EHR system designed and developed to operate on the cloud, maximizing the characteristics and benefits of cloud computing.

[2] Electronic health record information sharing service:

A system planned by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare to enable the sharing of patient electronic health record information among medical institutions and pharmacies nationwide.

[3] Fiscal year 2028:

Fujitsu Japan's fiscal year ends on March 31.

[4] 47% market share in the large hospital sector:

Calculated by Fujitsu Japan based on hospitals with 400 or more beds, as listed in the "Medical Device Systems White Paper 2026: List of Facilities with Hospital Information Systems (HIS)" from the Monthly New Medical Data Book series.

data.title: FMC downgraded at Jefferies as 'visibility deteriorates, again' with guidance cut
data.description:
FMC Corp. rebounded 1.7% in Friday's trading after plunging 31% in the previous session when the agricultural chemicals company slashed its Q3 revenue guidance to $65M-$125M, far below consensus estimates, with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $510M-$565M, compared to its previous outlook for positive $120M-$140M.

Following the guidance cut, Jefferies analysts Daniel Rizzo and Charles Boakye downgraded FMC shares to Hold from Buy with a new $5 price target, citing limited visibility, macro headwinds, and persistent pressure from generics.

The current crop protection market remains at a trough, and FMC moved to reduce pricing on a wide range of off-patent crop protection products and simplify its North American pricing strategy, no longer using the high-gross margin, high-rebate model; as a result, the company cut its Q3 revenue and EBITDA projections, Rizzo and Boakye said.

Commodity pricing pressures will likely persist through the 2027 growing seasons, the analysts said, estimating a ~10% pricing decline next year in the core portfolio—offsetting 1%-2% volume growth—with rynaxypyr posing another $100M headwind.

On the positive side, new products including biologicals likely remain on track, and the benefits from the footprint optimization likely will be evident by H2 2027, according to Rizzo and Boakye, adding that Fluindapyr continues to ramp, and Dodhylex and Isoflex are positioned for significant growth beginning in 2028.

data.title: Top global climate science body meet ends without deal on review timeline
data.description:
By Sudarshan Varadhan and Kate Abnett

The meeting of the members of the world's leading authority on climate change ended on Friday without an agreement on a timeline to publish its next review of the latest science on the warming planet, four sources familiar with the matter said.

The meeting of representatives to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change from its 195 member states in Ethiopia's capital, Addis Ababa, this week was seen by many as the last chance to agree publication dates before UN climate talks in November 2028, when governments are due to assess progress toward goals set in the 2015 Paris agreement.

The impasse, which has lasted nearly three years, could leave countries to decide the next phase of action without consensus on critical issues, including the extent to which some global warming might be reversible.

The IPCC did not immediately respond to a request seeking comment.

The dispute reflects deep rifts among wealthy industrialized nations, major emerging economies and poorer nations over how to respond to warming temperatures and how much of that burden should be shouldered by different countries.

The possibility that the IPCC's reports might not be ready in time for the 2028 climate talks has alarmed a coalition of 30 countries, including European, Latin American and small-island states pushing for immediate action.

However, countries including India, Kenya, Saudi Arabia, Russia and China are pressing for more time to prepare the IPCC's next reports to ensure scientists from less-resourced countries can make meaningful contributions.

The IPCC's reviews of the world's existing knowledge on climate change carry weight with governments because they are written by hundreds of international experts and approved by every member state.

Its reports are also used by governments to plan their responses to climate change and have been cited in international court rulings.

The UN Environment Programme has said repeatedly that global efforts to limit warming are falling short and that deeper emissions cuts are needed to avoid more extreme weather and climate-related disasters.
